{{Quote|''[The Priapulin]'' even tell time in terms of the tidal shifts of their world; one tidal hour equals ten galactic standard hours.|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species''|<ref name="TEGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>}}
'''Pria''' was a [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] that was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Priapulin]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. A tectonically active [[Waterworld/Legends|waterworld]], it featured [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] and polar [[Water/Legends|ice]] caps, with the majority of the Priapulin population living in atolls and tidal flats. Pria had a single [[Pria's sole moon|moon]], and its tidal cycles equalled almost exactly ten [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]], giving rise to the Priapulins using [[tidal hour]]s as a unit of [[Time/Legends|time]].

The Priapulin society was inherently cooperative, and they maintained [[Symbiosis/Legends|symbiotic]] relationships with several types of creatures of varying sentience&mdash;including the [[crast]]i, which served the Priapulins as [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] while using their [[Diet/Legends|digestive]] tracts in their [[Reproduction/Legends|reproductive]] cycle. The Priapulins were deeply pacifistic and also had a long history of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] travel, with Priapulin [[Starship/Legends|starships]] often being modified to support their aquatic physiology. Pria fell into a state of disrepair and neglect during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], but during the existence of its successor, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the Priapulins were rebuilding their homeworld.

==Description==
Pria was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Gamer8" /> located in the [[Pria system/Legends|Pria system]]. It lay in the [[Arrowhead]] region, a part of [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="TEA Pria" /> Pria was [[Orbit/Legends|circled]] by a single [[Pria's sole moon|moon]], which, according to the planet's [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] [[Priapulin]] [[Species/Legends|species]], maintained a "perfect" orbit. The [[Local day/Legends|local day]] on Pria lasted twenty [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] and three [[Standard second|seconds]].<ref name="Gamer8" />

[[File:Priapulin-TEGAS.png|thumb|left|300px|The Priapulins evolved on Pria.]]
Pria was a tectonically active [[Waterworld/Legends|waterworld]].<ref name="CSWE Pria" /> Its surface featured a chaotic collection of landmasses that were shifting and were affected by a rapid drift of tectonic plates, growth of polar [[Water/Legends|ice]] caps, and a cycle of ice ages, with [[Geologist/Legends|geologists]] estimating that the latter occurred every ten thousand [[Standard year/Legends|standard years]]. Pria had [[Salt/Legends|briny]] [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] along the bottoms of which ran trenches. At the surface level there were multiple atolls and tidal flats. In addition, early Priapulin explorations of dry sea beds were believed to have led to their adoption of the unit of distance known as [[salt pan]].<ref name="Gamer8" />

By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="Gamer8" /> which began in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> tidal cycles on Pria had for several [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] equaled nearly exactly ten standard hours. Meteorologically, Pria was a turbulent world, and its oceans were stormy and maelstrom-like. However, [[Temperature/Legends|temperatures]] on the planet were moderate, with the Priapulins consequently not being well-adapted for cool conditions. Pria's oceans were inhabited by a variety of fauna ranging from harmless to particularly [[Death/Legends|lethal]], and [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] theorized that the Priapulins had evolved from burrowing [[Priapulin precursor species|worm-like creatures]].<ref name="Gamer8" />

==History==
Some [[sentientologist]]s speculated that the Priapulin society's strict adherence to pacifism was a consequence of a near-catastrophe that almost caused the extinction of the species.<ref name="Gamer8" /> Long before the reign of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]],<ref name="TEGAS" /> which was [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|formed]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> the Priapulins developed [[Realspace/Legends|space]] travel,<ref name="TEGAS" /> and the species was known offworld<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> by [[990 BBY]].<ref name="TJP" /><ref name="JPEndnotes1">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2010/12/endnotes-for-star-wars-jedi-path-part-1.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Jedi Path (part 1 of 4)}}</ref> At some point by [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]],<ref name="29 BBY">{{GamerCite|8|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Priapulin}} dates [[Charza Kwinn]]'s departure from Pria to sometime prior to the events of ''[[Rogue Planet]]'', which ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' places in [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]].</ref> the Priapulin future [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Charza Kwinn]] left Pria at a relatively young age in order to find his destiny in the wider [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], eventually becoming an auxiliary of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="Gamer8" />

Significant portions of Pria fell into disrepair and neglect during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|rule]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]<ref name="Gamer8" /> that [[Declaration of a New Order|began]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="NEC" /> However, the Priapulins had begun the long process of rebuilding their homeworld by the time of the existence of the Empire's successor, the New Republic. At one point, a large contingent of crews allied with the New Republic and consisting primarily of members of aquatic species such as the [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]], the [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]], and the [[Kian'thar]] landed on the planet and submerged into Pria's [[North Flows]] in order to begin reparation work&mdash;an event that proved to be particularly inspiring.<ref name="Gamer8" /> Pria was also mentioned in an entry dedicated to the Priapulins in the [[Book/Legends|book]] ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', which was based on the notes of [[Senior Anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] and published during the New Republic's rule.<ref name="TEGAS" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Priapulin}}
{{Quote|As on their world, the system of teamwork ''[the Priapulins]'' maintain among their spaceship crews is distinctly symbiotic.|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species''|<ref name="TEGAS" />}}
Pria was the homeworld of the Priapulins, a species of sentient, [[Worm/Legends|worm]]-like<ref name="Gamer8" /> [[Gastropod/Legends|gastropod]]. The Priapulins reached four [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length on average<ref name="TEGAS" /> and spoke the [[Priap]] [[Language/Legends|language]].<ref name="Gamer8" /> Although the Priapulins were amphibious, they needed to be in water nearly constantly, being at risk of quickly dying if subjected to arid environments, with a room that a [[Human/Legends|Human]] would typically find to be comfortable being too dry for a Priapulin.<ref name="TEGAS" /> On Pria, the majority of the Priapulin population resided in atolls and tidal flats.<ref name="Gamer8" />

The Priapulins maintained a [[Symbiosis/Legends|symbiotic]] relationship with the [[crast]], a species of small, semi-sentient<ref name="Gamer8" /> [[Crab/Legends|crab]]-like<ref name="CSWE foodkin">{{CSWECite|I|285|food-kin}}</ref> [[Crustacean/Legends|crustacoids]]. The [[Reproduction/Legends|reproductive]] cycle of the crasti occurred partially within the [[Diet/Legends|digestive]] tract of a Priapulin: Priapulins ate [[Egg/Legends|egg]]-carrying adult crasti for [[Foodstuff/Legends|nourishment]] and then incubated their unborn young inside themselves. After a time, a Priapulin would regurgitate&mdash;and thus effectively give birth to<ref name="Gamer8" />&mdash;and care for<ref name="TEGAS" /> a new [[Litter (biology)|litter]] of crasti, thus ensuring the survival of the latter species and propagating the symbiotic cycle.<ref name="Gamer8" />

[[File:Priapaulin_G8.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A pair of Priapulin among members of other species]]
Similarly as with the crasti, the Priapulins established complex symbiotic relationships with several types of creatures, both non-sentient and near-sentient. Many of these beings assisted the Priapulins in daily tasks ranging from the management of community duties to [[Starship/Legends|starship]] operation and [[Navigator/Legends|navigation]]. Cooperation was a cornerstone of the Priapulin society, as was extreme pacifism, with members of the species abhorring violence. In addition, to the frequent confusion of non-Priapulins, Priapulin speech&mdash;even in the [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] language&mdash;commonly made use of Pria-specific terms such as "salt pan" for expressing travel distances and<ref name="Gamer8" /> [[tidal hour]]s<ref name="TEGAS" /> instead of standard hours as a unit of time.<ref name="Gamer8" />

The Priapulins had a long history of spaceflight, although their physiology frequently required special accommodations when offworld. Priapulin-owned starships were<ref name="Gamer8" /> uniquely<ref name="TEGAS" /> modified: similarly to their abodes, the vessels were damp and often had their floors covered in saltwater. Priapulin ships were also filled with [[Mollusk/Legends|mollusks]]<ref name="Gamer8" /> and living food.<ref name="TEGAS" />

==Locations==
Pria was the site of the underwater location known as the North Flows. In addition, the Priapulins established several outposts and research facilities along the planet's ocean floors and trenches.<ref name="Gamer8" />

==Behind the scenes==
Pria was introduced in the [[2001]] reference book [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']] by [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]].<ref name="TEGAS" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Pria [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the planet itself, in grid square M-10.<ref name="TEA Pria" />
